docs.title: samstars Documentation
docs.text: Multimodal individual tree crown segmentation from imagery and lidar-derived rasters.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
samstars is a Python package for instance segmentation of individual tree crowns from high-resolution imagery and lidar-derived rasters. The resulting crown polygons can be used for downstream species classification.

It combines:

  • high-resolution imagery (satellite, aerial, or drone)
  • lidar-derived raster layers (e.g., canopy height and density)

It automatically derives prompts from lidar structure and spectral cues to segment individual tree crowns with limited training annotations.

docs.title: First Segmentation
docs.text:
Use the model bundle created by Training with imagery and lidar rasters prepared as described in Data Preparation.

from pathlib import Path

from samstars import segment

result = segment(
    model=Path("/abs/path/model_bundle"),
    img=Path("/abs/path/image.tif"),
    chm=Path("/abs/path/chm.tif"),
    den=Path("/abs/path/first_return_density.tif"),
    out=Path("/abs/path/run_dir/segmentation_run"),
    storage="persistent",
    device="cpu",
)

print(result.crowns)

See Installation to install the library. For a minimal training and segmentation workflow, see Quick Start. For task-focused documentation, see Data Preparation, Training, Segmentation, and Downstream Analysis.

docs.title: Advanced Workflows
docs.text: These workflows support inspection, partial reruns, and direct use of component models. Use storage="persistent" to retain the files needed for them. The basic model-bundle workflow is covered in Training and Segmentation.

docs.title: Resume a Segmentation Run
docs.text:
Reuse the same model, inputs, and output directory:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars import segment

result = segment(
    model=Path("models/crowns"),
    tiles_dir=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    out=Path("runs/tiled_segmentation"),
    storage="persistent",
    stardist_resume=True,
    device="cpu",
)

Complete proposal rasters are skipped by default. stardist_resume=True also reuses completed refinement checkpoints. Resuming assumes that inputs and settings are unchanged. Use a new output directory when changing the model, band selections, or processing parameters.

Additional controls include:

Parameter Purpose skip_existing_sam=False Recompute proposal rasters. stardist_resume_from_labels=True Rebuild missing refinement checkpoints from saved label rasters; also requires stardist_resume=True. Recovered crowns have no confidence score. stardist_skip_sources="tile_a,tile_b" Skip named proposal sources. stardist_skip_sources_file=Path(...) Read source names to skip from a text file.

docs.title: Run One Stage at a Time
docs.text:
Use a persistent output directory to share proposals between stages:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars import segment

run = dict(
    model=Path("models/crowns"),
    tiles_dir=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    out=Path("runs/tiled_segmentation"),
    storage="persistent",
    device="cpu",
)

segment(**run, run_stardist=False)
segment(**run, run_sam=False)

The first call writes proposals; the second refines those proposals into crown polygons. For retraining refinement with new annotations, see Retrain Refinement for One Area.

docs.title: Proposal and Canopy Index Rasters
docs.text:
The proposal stage produces raster maps of likely crown regions for refinement into individual crown polygons. Persistent segmentation runs save these maps and their supporting rasters in out/proposals/rasters/, indexed by out/proposals/proposal_records.json.

The index is a JSON list with one record per processed tile or chip. Each record groups the corresponding raster paths below and may include spatial metadata in meta.

Record key Raster Contents file_name *_sam_prob.tif Smoothed crown-proposal probability. index *_sam_index.tif Canopy index used as the default refinement input. chm *_chm.tif Aligned canopy heights. cost *_cost.tif Aligned boundary and gap cues. logit *_logit.tif Cached proposal response before mosaic smoothing.

The canopy index combines proposal probability, normalized canopy height, boundary cost, and a ground-height weight. Higher values indicate stronger crown support.

train(...) and segment(...) create and use the index automatically. It connects proposal generation to refinement and is also used to build refinement training samples. To rerun refinement or retrain from saved proposals, retain the index and its referenced rasters at the recorded paths. Final crown polygons can be used independently of these intermediate files.

docs.title: Run Records and CHM Scaling
docs.text:
out/run_records/tiles.json indexes the prepared tiles. tiles.pending.json identifies tiles without complete proposal outputs. The high-level API creates both files automatically; CLI Scripts provides commands for rebuilding them individually.

When CHM is used as an auxiliary refinement channel, out/proposal_scale_stats.json stores the scaling limits used across proposal records. Training stores its corresponding statistics under model_bundle/_training/. These files are generated automatically.

docs.title: Inspect Training Chips
docs.text:
Training chips contain imagery arrays, crown masks, CHM arrays, and prompts. To rebuild them from labeled tiles independently:

python -m samstars.training.chips \
  --tiles-dir /abs/path/training_tiles \
  --out-dir /abs/path/training_chips

Each input tile needs img.tif, chm.tif, and crowns.gpkg. The output contains images/, masks/, chm/, and prompts/ subdirectories. train(...) performs this step automatically.

docs.title: Segment With Separate Model Files
docs.text:
run_segmentation(...) accepts a proposal-decoder checkpoint and a refinement model directory directly:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.segmentation import run_segmentation

run_segmentation(
    tiles_dir=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    out_dir=Path("runs/segmentation"),
    sam_ckpt=Path("models/decoder.pth"),
    stardist_model=Path("models/refinement"),
    device="cpu",
)

sam_ckpt is the trained proposal checkpoint. stardist_model is the model subdirectory containing config.json and its weights. This interface also accepts source img, chm, and den rasters with explicit band settings in place of tiles_dir.

docs.title: Multispectral Cost Settings
docs.text:
rgb_bands selects the three image channels in red, green, blue order. For standard eight-band WorldView-3 imagery, true-color RGB is (5, 3, 2). An optional near-infrared band adds the NDVI gap cue; a separate texture band can also be selected:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.features import build_cost_surface, write_cost_surface

cost, profile = build_cost_surface(
    img_path=Path("data/worldview3.tif"),
    chm_path=Path("data/chm.tif"),
    rgb_bands=(5, 3, 2),
    nir_band=7,
    texture_band=1,
)
write_cost_surface(cost, profile, Path("prepared/cost.tif"))

These explicit cost settings reproduce the earlier WorldView-3 height, NDVI, and coastal-band texture combination. The same band arguments are accepted by build_tiles(...), train(...), and segment(...). Red and near-infrared values should use comparable radiometric units for NDVI.

Earlier versions inferred (7, 5, 3) model channels from band count and assumed WorldView-3 bands for cost preparation. New preparation defaults to (1, 2, 3) and adds NDVI only when nir_band is specified. Existing models trained on other channel combinations need matching prepared inputs, or retraining with the new RGB settings. The former wv3_path keyword remains an alias for img_path; it no longer implies a band layout.

docs.title: Data Preparation
docs.text:
Data preparation requires imagery, a canopy height model (CHM), and a first-return density raster. samstars uses these to generate crown prompts and boundary cues that help separate neighboring crowns.

train(...) and segment(...) can create the cost surface and seed points automatically from these rasters. The examples below show how to create them separately for inspection, or prepare them together as tiles.

docs.title: Required Inputs
docs.text: Input What to provide img A georeferenced RGB or multiband imagery raster. chm A single-band raster of canopy height above ground, in meters. den A single-band raster of first lidar returns per cell, or per square meter. crowns One polygon per labeled tree crown, required only for training.

docs.title: Image Bands
docs.text:
rgb_bands identifies the red, green, and blue bands using one-based indices. The default (1, 2, 3) assumes the source image already has those bands in RGB order. For a BGR image, use rgb_bands=(3, 2, 1). For a multiband image, select the three corresponding source bands explicitly; the sensor is not inferred from band count.

An optional nir_band adds a near-infrared band for the NDVI cost cue. texture_band selects a separate band for image texture; by default, texture uses the mean of the selected RGB channels. These arguments are available in build_cost_surface(...), build_tiles(...), train(...), and segment(...). See Advanced Workflows for a multispectral example.

Prepared images contain the three selected RGB channels. Use the same channel content and cost settings during training and segmentation.

docs.title: Prepare Lidar Rasters
docs.text:
The CHM and first-return density raster can be derived from LAS/LAZ point clouds with any suitable processing tool:

  1. Height above ground. Normalize point heights using classified ground points or a terrain model.
  2. Canopy height model. Calculate the maximum height above ground in each raster cell.
  3. First-return density. Select points with ReturnNumber == 1 and count them in each raster cell. For returns per square meter, divide each count by the cell area in square meters.

Export both outputs as single-band GeoTIFFs. Keep density units and cell size consistent between training and segmentation, since seed detection uses the raster values directly.

For implementation details, see PDAL's height normalization and raster output tools, or the PyForestScan Python example.

docs.title: Align and Check the Rasters
docs.text:
• Use a projected coordinate system in meters and north-up imagery with square pixels.
  • Cover the same area in all three rasters and mark missing data as NoData.
  • Check that canopy features line up between the imagery and lidar rasters.

build_tiles(...), and the preparation performed by train(...) and segment(...), reproject and resample the CHM and density raster to the imagery grid. This matches coordinate systems and pixels; it does not correct positional offsets between surveys.

For the individual cost-surface and seed examples below, first align the rasters to the same CRS, pixel size, grid origin, and extent using your GIS software or Rasterio. These lower-level functions expect already aligned inputs.

docs.title: Create a Cost Surface
docs.text:
A cost surface is a raster with values from 0 to 1 that highlights likely crown boundaries. Higher values discourage grouping seed points across those areas and reduce segmentation scores there. For RGB imagery, it combines canopy-height changes and image texture. When nir_band is supplied, it also includes an NDVI cue for canopy gaps and non-vegetated areas. The weights of the available terms are rescaled to sum to one.

Create cost.tif from an aligned image and CHM:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.features import build_cost_surface, write_cost_surface

cost, profile = build_cost_surface(
    img_path=Path("data/image.tif"),
    chm_path=Path("data/chm.tif"),
    rgb_bands=(1, 2, 3),
)

write_cost_surface(cost, profile, Path("prepared/cost.tif"))

docs.title: Create Seed Points
docs.text:
Seed points are candidate tree-crown centers used as automatic prompts. The detector finds peaks in the CHM and first-return density raster, filters low-canopy points, and groups nearby candidates using the cost surface.

Using the cost raster created above:

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.features import SeedParams, canonical_seeds

params = SeedParams(
    chm_raster=Path("data/chm.tif"),
    den_raster=Path("data/first_return_density.tif"),
    cost_raster=Path("prepared/cost.tif"),
    min_canopy_height=2.0,
)

seeds = canonical_seeds(params)
seeds.to_file("prepared/seeds.gpkg", driver="GPKG")

min_canopy_height is in meters. Other useful SeedParams controls are:

Parameter Meaning d_min Minimum peak value, applied to both height and density rasters; default 4.5. Interpret this against the units of each raster. min_dist_px Peak-search radius in pixels; default 4. gauss_sigma Smoothing scale in pixels before finding peaks; default 2. merge_radius Controls grouping of nearby candidates using distance and cost; default 3.0 in projected coordinate units.

Overlay cost.tif and seeds.gpkg on the imagery in your GIS to inspect the boundary cues and candidate crown centers.

docs.title: Build Prepared Tiles
docs.text:
For large scenes or reusable inputs, build_tiles(...) aligns the rasters and generates the cost surface and seeds for each tile in one call. You can use this directly without running the individual examples above.

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.data import build_tiles

build_tiles(
    img=Path("data/image.tif"),
    chm=Path("data/chm.tif"),
    den=Path("data/first_return_density.tif"),
    out=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    rgb_bands=(1, 2, 3),
    tile=500.0,
    overlap=20.0,
)

tile and overlap use the imagery CRS units: with a CRS in meters, this creates approximately 500-meter tiles with 20 meters of overlap. The example assumes RGB imagery. If training used nir_band or texture_band, supply the same settings when building inference tiles.

Each tile directory contains:

File Contents img.tif The selected red, green, and blue bands, in that order. chm.tif Canopy heights on the tile grid. cost.tif Boundary cues and, when NIR is supplied, an NDVI gap cue. seeds.gpkg Candidate crown-center points.

Training tiles also need crowns.gpkg; see Training for preparing labeled tiles. See Large Raster Runs to run segmentation from the prepared tiles.

docs.title: Downstream Analysis
docs.text:
samstars writes individual crown polygons. Those polygons can be used as crown-level units for later analysis, including species classification, biomass estimation, crown metrics, and change analysis.

Species classification is a separate downstream step using these crown geometries.

docs.title: Crown Output
docs.text:
The main segmentation output is:

out/crowns/crowns.gpkg

The GeoPackage layer is named crowns. It contains one feature per predicted crown:

Field Description id Crown identifier within the output file. source Source tile or proposal record used to create the crown. label Internal instance label from polygon refinement. score Refinement confidence score when available. geometry Crown polygon in the output CRS.

If you combine outputs from multiple runs, add a run identifier before merging files so crown identifiers remain unambiguous.

docs.title: Species Classification
docs.text:
A common downstream workflow is:

  1. Run samstars.segment(...) to produce crowns.gpkg.
  2. Extract crown-level predictors from imagery, CHM, vegetation indices, texture layers, or other rasters.
  3. Train or apply a species classifier outside samstars, for example with XGBoost, scikit-learn, or another modeling library.
  4. Join predicted species labels and confidence scores back to the crown polygons.

Use a table with one row per crown and a stable key, usually id for one output file or run_id plus id for merged runs.

docs.title: Join Species Predictions
docs.text:
After classification, read the crown GeoPackage into a GeoPandas GeoDataFrame and join a prediction table to it.

from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

crowns_path = Path("/abs/path/segmentation_run/crowns/crowns.gpkg")
species_table = Path("/abs/path/species_predictions.csv")
out_path = Path("/abs/path/segmentation_run/crowns/crowns_with_species.gpkg")

crowns = gpd.read_file(crowns_path, layer="crowns")
species = pd.read_csv(species_table)

classified = crowns.merge(
    species[["id", "species", "species_score"]],
    on="id",
    how="left",
    validate="one_to_one",
)

classified.to_file(out_path, layer="crowns", driver="GPKG")

Recommended downstream fields:

Field Description species Predicted species name, code, or class label. species_score Classifier confidence or probability for the assigned class. species_model Optional classifier name or version. species_source Optional source of the species label, such as model, field label, or manual edit.

docs.title: Feature Tables
docs.text:
Feature extraction is project-specific. The crown polygons can be used with any raster or vector processing library that supports polygon summaries.

Typical crown-level predictors include:

  • image-band means, medians, and standard deviations
  • vegetation indices summarized inside each crown
  • CHM height summaries, such as maximum, mean, and percentiles
  • texture metrics computed from imagery or canopy-height rasters
  • crown geometry metrics, such as area and perimeter

docs.title: Quality Checks
docs.text:
Before using crown polygons for classification or other analyses, check:

  • the output CRS matches the rasters used for feature extraction
  • very small or low-confidence crowns are handled consistently
  • training and prediction areas are kept separate during model assessment
  • merged outputs have unique crown identifiers
  • species labels are joined to the correct segmentation run

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
These notebooks demonstrate workflows using your own imagery, lidar rasters, and annotations. Replace the paths in each notebook before running it. The source data and base checkpoint are supplied separately; see Data Preparation and Training.

Open a notebook with a Python environment containing samstars and Jupyter. The code uses the installed package and can run outside a repository checkout.

Notebook Purpose Train and Segment One Area Train on a labeled area and segment another area. Train and Segment a Tiled Area Train a bundle, prepare larger rasters as tiles, and segment them. Retrain Refinement for One Area Reuse saved proposals to train and run a replacement refinement model.

The first two notebooks show the essential settings first, with optional tuning at the end. For evaluation, use areas held out from training; the notebooks demonstrate execution of the workflow.

See Quick Start for a compact example and Advanced Workflows for intermediate files and partial reruns.

docs.title: Supported environments
docs.text:
The initial samstars release supports Python 3.10 through 3.12 on these 64-bit platforms:

Platform Baseline Optional acceleration Ubuntu 20.04 or newer on x86-64 CPU NVIDIA CUDA macOS 14 or newer on Apple Silicon CPU PyTorch MPS and TensorFlow Metal

CPU execution is the supported baseline and is used by the examples unless stated otherwise. Windows, Linux ARM64, and Intel macOS are not currently tested release targets.

docs.title: Install the library from PyPI
docs.text:
python -m pip install samstars

For optional GPU support, see NVIDIA CUDA on Linux or Apple Silicon acceleration.

On Linux, use PyTorch's CPU-only package index when you do not want pip to install NVIDIA runtime libraries:

python -m pip install "torch>=2.3,<3" "torchvision>=0.18,<1" \
  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
python -m pip install samstars

Verify:

python -c "import samstars, torch, tensorflow as tf; print('samstars import ok'); print('torch', torch.__version__); print('tensorflow', tf.__version__)"
pip show samstars

docs.title: NVIDIA CUDA on Linux
docs.text:
CUDA builds of PyTorch and Torchvision must be installed as a matched pair. Use the official PyTorch installation selector to install a pair within the supported ranges (torch>=2.3,<3 and torchvision>=0.18,<1), then install samstars:

# Run the command produced by the PyTorch selector first.
python -m pip install "tensorflow[and-cuda]>=2.15,<2.19"
python -m pip install samstars

The TensorFlow command follows the official TensorFlow pip guide and requires a compatible NVIDIA driver. If TensorFlow GPU support is not needed, omit that command and let samstars install standard TensorFlow. PyTorch and TensorFlow detect accelerators independently: device="cuda" controls proposal generation, while TensorFlow controls refinement. Set stardist_cpu=True when only proposal generation should use CUDA.

Check CUDA availability:

python - <<'PY'
import torch
import tensorflow as tf

print("torch:", torch.__version__)
print("cuda runtime:", torch.version.cuda)
print("cuda available:", torch.cuda.is_available())
print("device:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "none")
print("tensorflow:", tf.__version__)
print("tensorflow GPUs:", tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU"))
PY

Use device="cuda" only when torch.cuda.is_available() returns True.

docs.title: Apple Silicon acceleration
docs.text:
The standard Apple Silicon PyTorch build can use MPS when it is available. TensorFlow Metal support is optional; see Apple's TensorFlow acceleration guide for host requirements:

python -m pip install "samstars[metal]"

Check both frameworks after installation:

python - <<'PY'
import torch
import tensorflow as tf

print("mps built:", torch.backends.mps.is_built())
print("mps available:", torch.backends.mps.is_available())
print("tensorflow:", tf.__version__)
print("tensorflow GPUs:", tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU"))
PY

Use device="mps" only when torch.backends.mps.is_available() returns True. Otherwise, keep device="cpu". TensorFlow Metal availability does not change the PyTorch device setting.

docs.title: Conda development environments
docs.text:
The repository environment files provide platform-specific Python 3.10 CPU development baselines. From the repository root, use the file for your platform and then install the checkout in editable mode:

# Ubuntu x86-64
conda env create -f environment.ubuntu.samstars.yml
conda activate samstars
python -m pip install -e .

# Apple Silicon macOS
conda env create -f environment.macos.samstars.yml
conda activate samstars
python -m pip install -e .

For Apple Silicon development with TensorFlow Metal, replace the final command with python -m pip install -e ".[metal]". The Ubuntu environment pins CPU builds of PyTorch and Torchvision. For CUDA development, uninstall those two packages after creating the environment, run the matched installation command from the PyTorch selector, and then install the checkout:

python -m pip uninstall -y torch torchvision
# Run the matched CUDA command produced by the PyTorch selector.
python -m pip install -e .

Verify that torch.version.cuda is non-empty and torch.cuda.is_available() is True before selecting device="cuda".

docs.title: Large Raster Runs
docs.text: Large areas can be prepared as overlapping tiles and processed with one trained model bundle. This reduces the size of the rasters handled in each preparation and inference step.

docs.title: Build Tiles
docs.text:
Use the same band selections and cost settings as during training. The example below assumes RGB imagery without a near-infrared band.

from pathlib import Path

from samstars.data import build_tiles

build_tiles(
    img=Path("data/inference/image.tif"),
    chm=Path("data/inference/chm.tif"),
    den=Path("data/inference/first_return_density.tif"),
    out=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    rgb_bands=(1, 2, 3),
    tile=500.0,
    overlap=20.0,
)

tile and overlap use the imagery CRS units. With a CRS in meters, this prepares approximately 500-meter tiles with 20 meters of overlap. Each tile contains the four files described in Data Preparation.

docs.title: Segment Prepared Tiles
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from samstars import segment

result = segment(
    model=Path("models/crowns"),
    tiles_dir=Path("prepared/tiles"),
    out=Path("runs/tiled_segmentation"),
    storage="persistent",
    device="cpu",
)

print(result.crowns)

The combined crown polygons are written to runs/tiled_segmentation/crowns/crowns.gpkg.

docs.title: Choosing Tile Settings
docs.text: Use tiles large enough to include neighboring crowns, and reduce tile size if memory use becomes excessive. Increase overlap if crowns are truncated at tile edges. For memory-intensive refinement, stardist_window_size_m and stardist_window_overlap_m subdivide each prepared tile into smaller prediction windows. These controls use map units, normally meters.

docs.title: Overlap and Duplicate Crowns
docs.text:
Crowns from overlapping tiles or prediction windows can overlap in the combined output. Final deduplication is disabled by default (stardist_dedup_iou_thr=0.0). Set this parameter to a value between 0 and 1, such as 0.6, to retain the higher-scoring crown when a pair's intersection-over-union reaches the threshold. Lower thresholds remove more overlapping predictions and can also remove distinct neighboring crowns.

Inspect tile boundaries when choosing this setting. Deduplication removes matching polygons; it does not trim all remaining overlaps or guarantee one prediction per tree.

For resuming long runs and inspecting intermediate outputs, see Advanced Workflows.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This example trains a crown-segmentation model and applies it to a small area. Install the package using Installation, then replace the example paths with your own files.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Inputs
docs.text:
Training requires imagery, a canopy height model, a first-return density raster, and crown polygons. See Data Preparation for raster requirements and Prepare Crown Annotations for labeling guidance. Download the base checkpoint before training.

The example assumes a three-band image in red, green, blue order. Set rgb_bands to match your image; see Image Bands.

docs.title: 2. Train a Model
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from samstars import train

model = train(
    img=Path("data/training/image.tif"),
    chm=Path("data/training/chm.tif"),
    den=Path("data/training/first_return_density.tif"),
    crowns=Path("data/training/crowns.gpkg"),
    sam_base_ckpt=Path("models/sam_vit_l_0b3195.pth"),
    out=Path("models/crowns"),
    rgb_bands=(1, 2, 3),
    storage="persistent",
    device="cpu",
)

Training creates a reusable model directory at models/crowns. The Training guide covers labeled tiles and training controls.

docs.title: 3. Segment an Area
docs.text:
from samstars import segment

result = segment(
    model=model,
    img=Path("data/inference/image.tif"),
    chm=Path("data/inference/chm.tif"),
    den=Path("data/inference/first_return_density.tif"),
    out=Path("runs/segmentation"),
    storage="persistent",
    device="cpu",
)

print(result.crowns)

The input imagery should have the same band order as the training imagery; segmentation reuses the bundle's band settings. For later runs, replace model=model with model=Path("models/crowns").

Open runs/segmentation/crowns/crowns.gpkg in your GIS to inspect the predicted crown polygons. See Large Raster Runs for tiled segmentation and Downstream Analysis for species classification and other uses.

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text: Segmentation combines imagery, canopy height, and first-return density with a trained model bundle to produce individual crown polygons. samstars.segment(...) prepares automatic prompts, generates crown proposals, and refines them into separate crown instances.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
For a source-raster run, provide:

  • RGB or multiband imagery
  • canopy height and first-return density rasters covering the same area
  • a model bundle created with Training

See Data Preparation for raster alignment and band requirements.

def build_scale_stats_from_proposal_records(
    *,
    proposal_records: Path,
    out: Path,
    percentiles: tuple[float, float] = (2.0, 98.0),
    chm_key: str = "chm",
    nodata_values: tuple[float, ...] = (-9999.0, -32768.0),
) -> dict:
    """Build StarDist CHM scale stats from proposal records."""
    p_lo, p_hi = percentiles
    recs = json.load(open(proposal_records))
    if not isinstance(recs, list):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Proposal records must be a list: {proposal_records}")

    parts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    missing = 0
    for rec in recs:
        chm_path = rec.get(chm_key, "")
        if not chm_path:
            missing += 1
            continue
        p = _resolve_record_path(chm_path, proposal_records)
        if not p.exists():
            missing += 1
            continue
        with rasterio.open(p) as src:
            marr = src.read(1, masked=True).astype(np.float32)
        arr = np.asarray(marr.compressed(), dtype=np.float32)
        arr = arr[np.isfinite(arr)]
        if arr.size and nodata_values:
            for nv in nodata_values:
                arr = arr[arr != np.float32(nv)]
        if arr.size:
            parts.append(arr)

    if not parts:
        raise RuntimeError(f"No finite CHM values found in {proposal_records}")

    vals = np.concatenate(parts)
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(vals, [p_lo, p_hi])
    out_data = {
        "percentiles": [p_lo, p_hi],
        "chm_01": {"lo": float(lo), "hi": float(hi)},
        "source_proposal_records": str(proposal_records.resolve()),
        "records_total": int(len(recs)),
        "records_missing_or_unreadable_chm": int(missing),
    }
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(out_data, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
    return out_data

def scale_to_01(arr: np.ndarray, lo: float, hi: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scale to 01."""
    data = np.asarray(arr, np.float32)
    data = np.nan_to_num(data, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    if not np.isfinite(lo) or not np.isfinite(hi) or hi <= lo:
        return np.zeros_like(data, dtype=np.float32)
    data = np.clip(data, lo, hi)
    data = (data - lo) / (hi - lo)
    return np.clip(data, 0.0, 1.0).astype(np.float32)

def scale_to_u8_per_channel(img_hwc: np.ndarray, lo_hi: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scale to u8 per channel."""
    arr = np.asarray(img_hwc, np.float32)
    arr = np.nan_to_num(arr, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    if arr.ndim != 3:
        raise ValueError("scale_to_u8_per_channel expects HWC input")
    h, w, c = arr.shape
    if len(lo_hi) < c:
        raise ValueError("scale_to_u8_per_channel lo_hi length < channels")
    out = np.zeros((h, w, c), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i in range(c):
        lo, hi = lo_hi[i]
        if not np.isfinite(lo) or not np.isfinite(hi) or hi <= lo:
            continue
        ch = np.clip(arr[..., i], lo, hi)
        ch = (ch - lo) * 255.0 / (hi - lo)
        out[..., i] = np.clip(ch, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return out

                img_crs=img_crs,

                seed_gauss_sigma=seed_gauss_sigma,
                seed_min_samples=seed_min_samples,
                seed_merge_radius=seed_merge_radius,

                thin_seeds=thin_seeds,
                thin_dist=thin_dist,
                write_den=write_den,
                skip_existing=skip_existing,
            )
        finally:
            chm_ds.close()
            den_ds.close()
            if chm_raw is not chm_ds:
                chm_raw.close()
            if den_raw is not den_ds:
                den_raw.close()

    if not written:
        raise RuntimeError("No valid tile outputs generated from the provided inputs.")

    tile_dir = out / tile_name
    if crowns is not None:
        crowns = Path(crowns)
        if not crowns.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing crowns file: {crowns}")

    print("✓ Single-tile inputs written to", out.resolve())
    return out

class CostSurfaceWeights:
    """Weights for height edges, NDVI gaps, image texture, and experimental SLIC edges.

    Weights must be nonnegative and sum to one. Terms without a supplied
    NIR band or SLIC layer are omitted and the remaining weights are rescaled.

            raise ValueError("Weights must be finite and nonnegative.")

def build_cost_surface(
    *,
    img_path: str | Path | None = None,
    chm_path: str | Path,
    rgb_bands: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    nir_band: int | None = None,
    texture_band: int | None = None,
    wv3_path: str | Path | None = None,
    slic_path: str | Path | None = None,
    weights: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0),
    nodata_value: float = -9999.0,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict]:
    """Build a 0–1 crown-boundary cost raster from aligned imagery and canopy height.

    Args:
        img_path: Three-band RGB or multiband imagery raster.
        chm_path: Single-band canopy heights in meters, on the imagery grid.
        rgb_bands: One-based red, green, blue indices. Defaults to `(1, 2, 3)`.
        nir_band: Optional near-infrared band for the NDVI gap term. With no NIR
            band, the cost uses height edges and image texture only.
        texture_band: Optional image band for texture. Defaults to the mean of
            the selected RGB channels.
        wv3_path: Legacy alias for `img_path`; band choices are still explicit.
        slic_path: Experimental SLIC labels on the imagery grid.
        weights: Height-edge, NDVI-gap, texture, and SLIC weights. Unavailable
            terms are omitted and the remaining weights are rescaled to sum to one.
        nodata_value: Output value at pixels with missing input data.

    Returns:
        cost: Float32 array of boundary costs. Higher values indicate stronger cues.
        profile: Rasterio profile for the single-band output.
    """
    if (img_path is None) == (wv3_path is None):
        raise ValueError("Provide img_path (or its legacy alias wv3_path), but not both.")
    w = CostSurfaceWeights(*weights)

    with rasterio.open(img_path if img_path is not None else wv3_path) as src:
        rgb_bands = _resolve_image_bands(src.count, rgb_bands, nir_band, texture_band)
        rgb = src.read(rgb_bands, masked=True).astype(np.float32).filled(np.nan)
        texture = rgb.mean(axis=0) if texture_band is None else src.read(
            texture_band, masked=True
        ).astype(np.float32).filled(np.nan)
        nir = None if nir_band is None else src.read(
            nir_band, masked=True
        ).astype(np.float32).filled(np.nan)
        profile = src.profile.copy()
        profile["bounds"] = rasterio.transform.array_bounds(
            profile["height"], profile["width"], profile["transform"]
        )

    chm, chm_profile = _read_band(chm_path)
    if (chm.shape != rgb.shape[1:] or chm_profile["crs"] != profile["crs"]
            or chm_profile["transform"] != profile["transform"]):
        raise ValueError("Imagery and CHM must have the same CRS, transform, and shape.")

    grad = _chm_gradient(chm)
    gap = 0.0 if nir is None else _normalise(1 - _ndvi(rgb[0], nir))
    tex = _texture_entropy(texture)
    valid = np.isfinite(chm) & np.isfinite(rgb).all(axis=0) & np.isfinite(texture)
    if nir is not None:
        valid &= np.isfinite(nir)

    if slic_path:
        if str(slic_path).lower().endswith(".gpkg"):
            slic_lab = _rasterise_slic_gpkg(slic_path, profile)
        else:                                  # assume raster label image
            slic_lab, _ = _read_band(slic_path)
        edge = _slic_edge(slic_lab)
    else:
        edge = 0.0

    w_gap = w.gap if nir is not None else 0.0
    w_slic = w.slic if slic_path is not None else 0.0
    total_weight = w.grad + w_gap + w.tex + w_slic
    if total_weight <= 0:
        raise ValueError("At least one available cost term must have a positive weight.")

    cost = (
        w.grad * grad +
        w_gap  * gap  +
        w.tex  * tex  +
        w_slic * edge
    ) / total_weight
    cost = np.clip(cost, 0, 1).astype(np.float32)

    cost[~valid | ~np.isfinite(cost)] = nodata_value
    profile.update(count=1, dtype="float32",
                   compress="deflate",
                   nodata=nodata_value)
    return cost, profile

def build_sparse_cost_graph(xs: np.ndarray,
                            ys: np.ndarray,
                            cost: np.ndarray,
                            tfm,
                            weight: float,
                            xy_thresh: float,
                            merge_radius: float,
                            samples: int = 8) -> "coo_matrix":
    """Build sparse cost graph."""
    n = len(xs)
    kd = cKDTree(np.c_[xs, ys])
    rows, cols, data = [], [], []
    ts = np.linspace(0., 1., samples + 2, dtype=np.float32)[1:-1]

    search_r = merge_radius + xy_thresh + 1e-6
    for i in range(n):
        xi, yi = xs[i], ys[i]
        neigh = kd.query_ball_point([xi, yi], search_r)
        neigh = [j for j in neigh if j > i]

        for j in neigh:
            dx, dy = xs[j] - xi, ys[j] - yi
            xy_dist = math.hypot(dx, dy)
            if xy_dist == 0.:
                continue

            if xy_dist <= xy_thresh or weight == 0.:
                d_eff = xy_dist
            else:
                xs_line = xi + ts * dx
                ys_line = yi + ts * dy
                rr, cc = rowcol(tfm, xs_line, ys_line, op=float)
                rr = np.clip(rr.round().astype(int), 0, cost.shape[0] - 1)
                cc = np.clip(cc.round().astype(int), 0, cost.shape[1] - 1)
                mean_cost = cost[rr, cc].mean()
                d_eff = xy_dist * (1. + weight * mean_cost)

            if d_eff <= merge_radius:
                rows.extend((i, j)); cols.extend((j, i))
                data.extend((d_eff, d_eff))

    return coo_matrix((data, (rows, cols)), shape=(n, n)).tocsr()

    """Detect CHM and density peaks and return one point per candidate cluster.

    Args:
        params: Raster paths and detection controls. Rasters must share a CRS,
            pixel grid, and extent; use a projected CRS in meters.

    Returns:
        A GeoDataFrame with id and geometry columns in the input CRS. Save it
        with to_file to create seeds.gpkg. Raises SystemExit if no candidates
        survive detection and canopy-height filtering.
    """
    chm_peaks = detect_peaks(params.chm_raster, "chm",
                             params.d_min, params.min_dist_px, params.gauss_sigma)
    den_peaks = detect_peaks(params.den_raster, "den",
                             params.d_min, params.min_dist_px, params.gauss_sigma)

    seeds = gpd.GeoDataFrame(pd.concat([chm_peaks, den_peaks], ignore_index=True),
                             geometry="geometry", crs=chm_peaks.crs)
    if seeds.empty:
        sys.exit("No seeds after CHM & density sampling.")

    seeds["x"], seeds["y"] = seeds.geometry.x, seeds.geometry.y
    seeds["canopy_height"] = _sample_raster_values(
        params.chm_raster,
        seeds["x"].to_numpy(),
        seeds["y"].to_numpy(),
    )
    seeds = seeds[np.isfinite(seeds["canopy_height"])]
    seeds = seeds[seeds["canopy_height"] >= params.min_canopy_height].reset_index(drop=True)
    if seeds.empty:
        sys.exit(
            "No seeds after applying the CHM canopy-height filter "
            f"(min_canopy_height={params.min_canopy_height})."
        )

    pts_xy = seeds[["x", "y"]].values

    kd = cKDTree(pts_xy)
    cluster = -np.ones(len(seeds), dtype=int)
    cid = 0
    for i in range(len(seeds)):
        if cluster[i] != -1:
            continue
        eps = float(np.clip(params.eps_scale * seeds.height.iloc[i],
                            params.min_eps, params.max_eps))
        idx = kd.query_ball_point(pts_xy[i], eps)
        if params.z_thresh >= 0 and np.ptp(seeds.height.iloc[idx]) > params.z_thresh:
            continue
        if len(idx) >= params.min_samples:
            cluster[idx] = cid
            cid += 1
    seeds["cluster1"] = cluster

    with rasterio.open(params.cost_raster) as src:
        cost = src.read(1).astype(np.float32)
        nodata = src.nodatavals[0] if src.nodatavals[0] is not None else np.nan
        cost[cost == nodata] = 1.0
        tfm = src.transform

    xs, ys = seeds["x"].values, seeds["y"].values
    G = build_sparse_cost_graph(xs, ys, cost, tfm,
                                params.cost_weight,
                                params.xy_thresh,
                                params.merge_radius,
                                samples=params.samples)

    if params.debug_dist and G.nnz:
        print(f"d_eff  min/median/max = "
              f"{G.data.min():.2f} / {np.median(G.data):.2f} / {G.data.max():.2f}")

    db2 = DBSCAN(eps=params.merge_radius, min_samples=1,
                 metric="precomputed", n_jobs=-1).fit(G)
    seeds["cluster"] = db2.labels_

    # optional height‑based split inside a cluster
    if params.dz_merge > 0:
        new_cl = np.empty_like(seeds["cluster"])
        new_id = 0
        for old_id, sub in seeds.groupby("cluster"):
            if np.ptp(sub.height) <= params.dz_merge:
                new_cl[sub.index] = new_id
                new_id += 1
            else:
                mid = sub.height.median()
                lo = sub[sub.height <= mid].index
                hi = sub[sub.height >  mid].index
                for idx in (lo, hi):
                    if idx.size:
                        new_cl[idx] = new_id
                        new_id += 1
        seeds["cluster"] = new_cl


    centres = (seeds
               .groupby("cluster", as_index=False)
               .agg(x=("x", "mean"),
                    y=("y", "mean"),
                    height=("height", "max")))
    centres["id"] = np.arange(len(centres))

    gdf_centres = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        centres,
        geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(centres.x, centres.y),
        crs=seeds.crs
    )[["id", "geometry"]]
    return gdf_centres

def detect_peaks(raster_path: Path | str,
                 origin: str,
                 d_min: float,
                 min_dist_px: int,
                 sigma: int = 0) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
    """Detect peaks."""
    raster_path = Path(raster_path)
    if not raster_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(raster_path)

    with rasterio.open(raster_path) as src:
        arr = src.read(1, masked=True).astype(np.float32).filled(np.nan)
        tfm, crs = src.transform, src.crs

    if sigma > 0:
        arr = gaussian_filter(arr, sigma=sigma)

    mask_local_max = arr == maximum_filter(arr, size=2 * min_dist_px + 1)
    peaks = np.logical_and(mask_local_max, arr >= d_min)
    rows, cols = np.where(peaks)
    xs, ys = xy(tfm, rows, cols, offset="center")
    heights = arr[rows, cols]

    return gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        dict(id=np.arange(rows.size),
             height=heights,
             origin=origin),
        geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(xs, ys),
        crs=crs
    )

def run_segmentation(
    *,
    tiles_dir: Path | None = None,
    img: Path | None = None,
    chm: Path | None = None,
    den: Path | None = None,
    rgb_bands: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    nir_band: int | None = None,
    texture_band: int | None = None,
    out_dir: Path,
    sam_ckpt: Path,
    device: str = "cpu",
    stardist_model: Path | None = None,
    stardist_input_key: str = "index",
    stardist_use_aux: bool = True,
    stardist_prob_thr: float | None = None,
    stardist_nms_thr: float | None = None,
    stardist_window_size_m: float | None = None,
    stardist_window_overlap_m: float = 0.0,
    stardist_dedup_iou_thr: float = 0.0,
    stardist_cpu: bool = False,
    stardist_resume: bool = False,
    stardist_resume_from_labels: bool = False,
    stardist_skip_sources: str | None = None,
    stardist_skip_sources_file: Path | None = None,
    run_sam: bool = True,
    run_stardist: bool = True,
    skip_existing_sam: bool = True,
    log_refinement: bool = False,
    fast: bool = True,
    fast_batch_size: int = 32,
    crop_smooth_sigma: float = 2.0,
    smooth_sigma: float = 4.0,
    post_smooth_sigma: float = 0.0,
) -> dict:
    """Run segmentation with separate proposal and refinement model paths.

    Supply tiles_dir for prepared inputs, or img/chm/den for automatic preparation.
    rgb_bands uses one-based red, green, blue indices, defaulting to (1, 2, 3).
    nir_band enables the NDVI cost term; texture_band optionally selects the
    texture source instead of mean RGB intensity.

    sam_ckpt is the trained proposal checkpoint. stardist_model points directly
    to the refinement directory containing config.json and weights.
    out_dir retains intermediates and final crowns. The return dictionary contains
    the run-record, proposal, and crown paths.

    Stage, threshold, resume, and window controls have the meanings documented
    by samstars.segment. Final polygon deduplication is disabled by default.
    """
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    resolved_sam_ckpt: Path | None = None
    resolved_stardist_model: Path | None = None

    raw_inputs = (img, chm, den)
    if tiles_dir is not None and any(v is not None for v in raw_inputs):
        raise ValueError("Provide either tiles_dir or img/chm/den, not both.")
    if tiles_dir is None:
        if any(v is None for v in raw_inputs):
            raise ValueError("Provide either tiles_dir or all of img/chm/den.")
        prepared_root = out_dir / "prep" / "scene"
        tiles_dir = build_single_tile(
            img=Path(img),
            chm=Path(chm),
            den=Path(den),
            rgb_bands=rgb_bands,
            nir_band=nir_band,
            texture_band=texture_band,
            out=prepared_root,
            skip_existing=True,
        )
    tiles_dir = Path(tiles_dir)

    records_root = out_dir / "run_records"
    proposals_root = out_dir / "proposals"
    crowns_dir = out_dir / "crowns"
    proposal_records = proposals_root / "proposal_records.json"
    proposal_rasters_dir = proposals_root / "rasters"
    tile_records = records_root / "tiles.json"
    pending_tile_records_path = records_root / "tiles.pending.json"
    recs, _ = build_tile_records(
        tiles_dir=tiles_dir,
        out_root=records_root,
    )

    pending_count = len(recs)
    active_tile_records = tile_records
    resolved_sam_ckpt = _resolve_sam_ckpt(sam_ckpt=sam_ckpt)
    if run_sam and skip_existing_sam:
        proposal_rasters_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _, _, pending_count = build_pending_tile_records(
            records_path=tile_records,
            proposal_rasters_dir=proposal_rasters_dir,
            out_path=pending_tile_records_path,
        )
        if pending_count > 0:
            active_tile_records = pending_tile_records_path

    if run_sam and (not skip_existing_sam or pending_count > 0):
        from samstars.segmentation.proposals import run_tile_proposals

        run_tile_proposals(
            active_tile_records,
            proposals_root,
            resolved_sam_ckpt,
            device=device,
            rgb_lo_hi=None,
            fast=fast,
            fast_batch=fast_batch_size,
            crop_smooth_sigma=crop_smooth_sigma,
            smooth_sigma=smooth_sigma,
            post_smooth_sigma=post_smooth_sigma,
        )

    _normalize_record_paths(proposal_records)
    proposal_records_rebuilt = False

    if not run_stardist:
        return {
            "records_root": records_root,
            "proposals_root": proposals_root,
            "crowns_dir": crowns_dir,
            "proposal_records": proposal_records,
        }

    if proposal_rasters_dir.exists():
        partial = _complete_proposal_records_from_rasters(proposal_rasters_dir)
        existing_count = _record_count(proposal_records)
        if partial and existing_count != len(partial):
            proposal_records.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            json.dump(partial, open(proposal_records, "w"))
            _normalize_record_paths(proposal_records)
            proposal_records_rebuilt = True

    if not proposal_records.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f"Missing proposal records: {proposal_records}")

    stardist_model_dir, stardist_model_name = _resolve_stardist_model(stardist_model=stardist_model)
    resolved_stardist_model = Path(stardist_model_dir) / stardist_model_name

    scale_stats = out_dir / "proposal_scale_stats.json"
    if proposal_records_rebuilt and scale_stats.exists():
        scale_stats.unlink()
    if not scale_stats.exists():
        build_scale_stats_from_proposal_records(
            proposal_records=proposal_records,
            out=scale_stats,
            percentiles=(2.0, 98.0),
            chm_key="chm",
            nodata_values=(-9999.0,),
        )

    refinement_py = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "refinement.py"
    cmd = [
        sys.executable,
        str(refinement_py),
        "--proposal-records",
        str(proposal_records),
        "--model-dir",
        str(Path(stardist_model_dir)),
        "--model-name",
        stardist_model_name,
        "--out-dir",
        str(crowns_dir),
        "--input-key",
        stardist_input_key,
        "--preds-name",
        "crowns.gpkg",
        "--write-labels",
    ]
    if stardist_use_aux:
        cmd.extend(
            [
                "--use-aux",
                "--scale-stats",
                str(scale_stats),
            ]
        )
    if (stardist_prob_thr is None) ^ (stardist_nms_thr is None):
        raise ValueError("Provide both stardist_prob_thr and stardist_nms_thr, or neither.")
    if stardist_window_size_m is not None and stardist_window_size_m <= 0:
        raise ValueError("stardist_window_size_m must be > 0.")
    if stardist_window_overlap_m < 0:
        raise ValueError("stardist_window_overlap_m must be >= 0.")
    if (
        stardist_window_size_m is not None
        and stardist_window_overlap_m >= stardist_window_size_m
    ):
        raise ValueError("stardist_window_overlap_m must be smaller than stardist_window_size_m.")
    if not (0.0 <= stardist_dedup_iou_thr < 1.0):
        raise ValueError("stardist_dedup_iou_thr must be in [0, 1).")
    if stardist_resume_from_labels and not stardist_resume:
        raise ValueError("stardist_resume_from_labels requires stardist_resume.")
    if stardist_prob_thr is not None and stardist_nms_thr is not None:
        cmd.extend(
            [
                "--prob-thr",
                str(stardist_prob_thr),
                "--nms-thr",
                str(stardist_nms_thr),
            ]
        )
    if stardist_window_size_m is not None:
        cmd.extend(
            [
                "--window-size-m",
                str(stardist_window_size_m),
                "--window-overlap-m",
                str(stardist_window_overlap_m),
            ]
        )
    if stardist_dedup_iou_thr > 0:
        cmd.extend(
            [
                "--dedup-iou-thr",
                str(stardist_dedup_iou_thr),
            ]
        )
    if log_refinement:
        cmd.append("--log")
    if stardist_resume:
        cmd.append("--resume")
    if stardist_resume_from_labels:
        cmd.append("--resume-from-labels")
    if stardist_skip_sources:
        cmd.extend(["--skip-sources", stardist_skip_sources])
    if stardist_skip_sources_file is not None:
        cmd.extend(["--skip-sources-file", str(stardist_skip_sources_file)])
    env = None
    if stardist_cpu:
        env = dict(**os.environ)
        env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = ""
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, env=env)

    return {
        "records_root": records_root,
        "proposals_root": proposals_root,
        "crowns_dir": crowns_dir,
        "proposal_records": proposal_records,
        "scale_stats": scale_stats,
        "sam_ckpt": resolved_sam_ckpt,
        "stardist_model": resolved_stardist_model,
    }

def prob_from_logit_seedcenter(logit: np.ndarray, seed_rc: tuple[int, int], res: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Prob from logit seedcenter."""
    logit = np.asarray(logit, np.float32)
    prob = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(LOGIT_SCALE * logit, -12, 12)))
    rr, cc = seed_rc
    yy, xx = np.indices(prob.shape)
    d_m = np.hypot(yy - rr, xx - cc) * res
    core_w = np.exp(-(d_m ** 2) / (2.0 * (CORE_SIGMA ** 2))) ** CORE_GAMMA
    prob *= core_w / (core_w.max() + 1e-6)
    return prob.astype(np.float32)

def process_chip(
    rec: dict,
    predictor: SamPredictor,
    device: str,
    rgb_lo_hi=None,
    fast: bool = False,
    fast_batch: int = 32,
    crop_smooth_sigma: float = CROP_SMOOTH_SIGMA,
    smooth_sigma: float = SMOOTH_SIGMA,
    post_smooth_sigma: float = POST_SMOOTH_SIGMA,
):
    """Process chip."""
    img_path = Path(rec["img_path"])
    name = f"{rec['tile']}_{rec['chip_id']}"
    chm_path = img_path.parent / "chm.tif"
    cost_path = img_path.parent / "cost.tif"
    seeds_path = img_path.parent / "seeds.gpkg"

    x0, y0, x1, y1 = rec["window"]
    win = Window(x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0)

    # --- Read imagery + aux rasters for this chip window ---
    with rasterio.open(img_path) as src:
        if src.count != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                "Prepared img.tif must contain three selected image channels. "
                "Prepare source imagery with build_tiles(rgb_bands=...)."
            )
        rgb = src.read((1, 2, 3), window=win, boundless=True, fill_value=0).astype(np.float32)
        tfm = rasterio.windows.transform(win, src.transform)
        crs = src.crs
        res = abs(tfm.a)
        H, W = int(win.height), int(win.width)

    with rasterio.open(chm_path) as csrc:
        CHM = csrc.read(1, window=win, boundless=True, fill_value=0).astype(np.float32)
    with rasterio.open(cost_path) as cosrc:
        COST = cosrc.read(1, window=win, boundless=True, fill_value=0).astype(np.float32)

    seeds = gpd.read_file(seeds_path).to_crs(crs)
    bounds_poly = box_from_window(win, tfm)
    seeds = seeds[seeds.intersects(bounds_poly)]
    if seeds.empty:
        return None
    print(f"seeds in chip: {len(seeds)}")

    # CHM blur for boost (within this chip window)
    sigma_px = SIGMA_METRE / max(res, 1e-9)
    chm_blur = gaussian_filter(CHM, sigma_px, mode="nearest")

    # Convert RGB to uint8 for SAM
    rgb_hwc = rgb.transpose(1, 2, 0)  # HWC float32
    if rgb_lo_hi is not None and len(rgb_lo_hi) >= rgb_hwc.shape[2]:
        RGB_u8 = scale_to_u8_per_channel(rgb_hwc, rgb_lo_hi[: rgb_hwc.shape[2]])
    else:
        RGB_u8 = np.stack([stretch_u8_percentile(rgb_hwc[..., c]) for c in range(rgb_hwc.shape[2])], axis=-1)
    if np.random.rand() < 0.05:
        sat0 = float((RGB_u8 == 0).mean())
        sat255 = float((RGB_u8 == 255).mean())
        print(f"{name}: RGB_u8 saturation 0={sat0:.3f} 255={sat255:.3f}")

    prob_mosaic = np.zeros((H, W), np.float32)

    # Group seeds by crop window within each chip
    hp_px = int(round(CONTEXT_FCTR * BOX_METRE / max(res, 1e-9)))
    hb = BOX_METRE / (2 * max(res, 1e-9))  # half box width in pixels

    if fast:
        # Fast mode: set image once per chip, batch prompts across seeds.
        predictor.set_image(RGB_u8)

        seed_infos = []
        for _, row in seeds.iterrows():
            r_arr, c_arr = rowcol(tfm, [row.geometry.x], [row.geometry.y])
            r, c = int(r_arr[0]), int(c_arr[0])
            r0, r1 = max(r - hp_px, 0), min(r + hp_px, H)
            c0, c1 = max(c - hp_px, 0), min(c + hp_px, W)
            if r1 <= r0 or c1 <= c0:
                continue

            chm_patch = CHM[r0:r1, c0:c1]
            rp, cp = (r - r0), (c - c0)

            # Foreground extra points: top CHM pixels inside the box
            mask_fg = chm_patch > CHM_GROUND
            yy, xx = np.where(mask_fg)
            in_box = ((np.abs(xx - cp) <= hb) & (np.abs(yy - rp) <= hb))
            yy, xx = yy[in_box], xx[in_box]
            if yy.size:
                keep = min(FG_EXTRA, yy.size)
                top_idx = np.argpartition(chm_patch[yy, xx], -keep)[-keep:]
                fg_pts = np.column_stack([xx[top_idx], yy[top_idx]])
                fg_pts = fg_pts + np.array([c0, r0], dtype=np.float32)
            else:
                fg_pts = np.empty((0, 2), np.float32)

            pts = np.vstack(([[c, r]], fg_pts)).astype(np.float32)
            lbl = np.hstack((np.array([1], np.int64), np.ones(len(fg_pts), np.int64)))

            # Negatives: ground
            yg, xg = np.where(chm_patch < CHM_GROUND)
            if len(yg) > NEG_MAX_GND:
                sel = np.random.choice(len(yg), NEG_MAX_GND, replace=False)
                yg, xg = yg[sel], xg[sel]
            neg_g = np.column_stack([xg, yg]).astype(np.float32)
            if neg_g.size:
                neg_g += np.array([c0, r0], dtype=np.float32)

            # Negatives: canopy outside the box
            yc, xc = np.where(chm_patch > CHM_GROUND)
            mask_out = ((np.abs(xc - cp) > hb) | (np.abs(yc - rp) > hb))
            yc, xc = yc[mask_out], xc[mask_out]
            if len(yc) > NEG_MAX_CAN:
                sel = np.random.choice(len(yc), NEG_MAX_CAN, replace=False)
                yc, xc = yc[sel], xc[sel]
            neg_c = np.column_stack([xc, yc]).astype(np.float32)
            if neg_c.size:
                neg_c += np.array([c0, r0], dtype=np.float32)

            if neg_g.size or neg_c.size:
                pts = np.vstack([pts, neg_g, neg_c])
                lbl = np.hstack([lbl, np.zeros(len(neg_g) + len(neg_c), np.int64)])

            seed_infos.append(
                {
                    "r": r,
                    "c": c,
                    "r0": r0,
                    "r1": r1,
                    "c0": c0,
                    "c1": c1,
                    "pts": pts,
                    "lbl": lbl,
                }
            )

        for i in range(0, len(seed_infos), max(1, fast_batch)):
            chunk = seed_infos[i : i + max(1, fast_batch)]
            if not chunk:
                continue

            pts_list = [c["pts"] for c in chunk]
            lbl_list = [c["lbl"] for c in chunk]
            boxes = [[c["c"] - hb, c["r"] - hb, c["c"] + hb, c["r"] + hb] for c in chunk]

            max_n = max(p.shape[0] for p in pts_list)
            pad_coord = np.array([[-10.0, -10.0]], np.float32)
            for j in range(len(pts_list)):
                need = max_n - pts_list[j].shape[0]
                if need:
                    pts_list[j] = np.vstack([pts_list[j], np.repeat(pad_coord, need, axis=0)])
                    lbl_list[j] = np.hstack([lbl_list[j], np.full(need, -1, np.int64)])

            pts_arr = torch.as_tensor(np.stack(pts_list), device=device)
            lbl_arr = torch.as_tensor(np.stack(lbl_list), device=device)
            boxes_t = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(boxes, np.float32), device=device)

            orig_hw = (H, W)
            pts_in = predictor.transform.apply_coords_torch(pts_arr, orig_hw)
            boxes_in = predictor.transform.apply_boxes_torch(boxes_t, orig_hw)

            with torch.inference_mode():
                _, _, low_res_logits = predictor.predict_torch(
                    point_coords=pts_in,
                    point_labels=lbl_arr,
                    boxes=boxes_in,
                    multimask_output=False,
                    return_logits=True,
                )

            for info, low_res in zip(chunk, low_res_logits):
                r0, r1, c0, c1 = info["r0"], info["r1"], info["c0"], info["c1"]
                h_p, w_p = r1 - r0, c1 - c0

                if low_res.dim() == 2:
                    low_res = low_res.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
                elif low_res.dim() == 3:
                    low_res = low_res.unsqueeze(0)
                logit_full = F.interpolate(low_res, (H, W), mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)[0, 0]
                logit = logit_full[r0:r1, c0:c1].detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)

                if crop_smooth_sigma > 0:
                    logit = gaussian_filter(logit, crop_smooth_sigma, mode="nearest")

                chm_patch = CHM[r0:r1, c0:c1]
                chm_blur_p = chm_blur[r0:r1, c0:c1]
                rr, cc = (info["r"] - r0), (info["c"] - c0)
                seed_h = chm_patch[rr, cc]
                dh = np.clip(chm_blur_p - seed_h, 0, None)
                dh_max = float(np.nanmax(dh)) if np.isfinite(dh).any() else 0.0
                if dh_max > 0:
                    logit = logit + (CHM_BOOST * dh / (dh_max + 1e-6)).astype(np.float32)

                seed_rc = (rr, cc)
                prob = prob_from_logit_seedcenter(logit, seed_rc=seed_rc, res=res)
                if np.random.rand() < 0.01:
                    print("seed prob pcts:", np.percentile(prob, [0, 50, 90, 99, 100]))

                prob_mosaic[r0:r1, c0:c1] = np.maximum(prob_mosaic[r0:r1, c0:c1], prob.astype(np.float32))
    else:
        buckets: dict[tuple[int, int, int, int], list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
        for _, row in seeds.iterrows():
            r_arr, c_arr = rowcol(tfm, [row.geometry.x], [row.geometry.y])
            r, c = int(r_arr[0]), int(c_arr[0])
            r0, r1 = max(r - hp_px, 0), min(r + hp_px, H)
            c0, c1 = max(c - hp_px, 0), min(c + hp_px, W)
            buckets.setdefault((r0, r1, c0, c1), []).append((r, c))

        for (r0, r1, c0, c1), pts_seed in buckets.items():
            h_p, w_p = r1 - r0, c1 - c0
            if h_p <= 0 or w_p <= 0:
                continue

            # Set SAM image for this crop
            predictor.set_image(RGB_u8[r0:r1, c0:c1])

            chm_patch = CHM[r0:r1, c0:c1]
            chm_blur_p = chm_blur[r0:r1, c0:c1]

            # Build prompts for each seed in this crop (batched)
            boxes, pts_list, lbl_list = [], [], []
            hb = BOX_METRE / (2 * max(res, 1e-9))  # half box width in pixels (crop coordinates)

            for (r, c) in pts_seed:
                rp, cp = (r - r0), (c - c0)
                boxes.append([cp - hb, rp - hb, cp + hb, rp + hb])

                # Foreground extra points: top CHM pixels inside the box
                mask_fg = chm_patch > CHM_GROUND
                yy, xx = np.where(mask_fg)
                in_box = ((np.abs(xx - (c - c0)) <= hb) & (np.abs(yy - (r - r0)) <= hb))
                yy, xx = yy[in_box], xx[in_box]
                if yy.size:
                    keep = min(FG_EXTRA, yy.size)
                    top_idx = np.argpartition(chm_patch[yy, xx], -keep)[-keep:]
                    fg_pts = np.column_stack([xx[top_idx], yy[top_idx]])
                else:
                    fg_pts = np.empty((0, 2), np.float32)

                pts = np.vstack(([[cp, rp]], fg_pts)).astype(np.float32)
                lbl = np.hstack((np.array([1], np.int64), np.ones(len(fg_pts), np.int64)))

                # Negatives: ground
                yg, xg = np.where(chm_patch < CHM_GROUND)
                if len(yg) > NEG_MAX_GND:
                    sel = np.random.choice(len(yg), NEG_MAX_GND, replace=False)
                    yg, xg = yg[sel], xg[sel]
                neg_g = np.column_stack([xg, yg]).astype(np.float32)

                # Negatives: canopy outside the box
                yc, xc = np.where(chm_patch > CHM_GROUND)
                mask_out = ((np.abs(xc - (c - c0)) > hb) | (np.abs(yc - (r - r0)) > hb))
                yc, xc = yc[mask_out], xc[mask_out]
                if len(yc) > NEG_MAX_CAN:
                    sel = np.random.choice(len(yc), NEG_MAX_CAN, replace=False)
                    yc, xc = yc[sel], xc[sel]
                neg_c = np.column_stack([xc, yc]).astype(np.float32)

                if neg_g.size or neg_c.size:
                    pts = np.vstack([pts, neg_g, neg_c])
                    lbl = np.hstack([lbl, np.zeros(len(neg_g) + len(neg_c), np.int64)])

                pts_list.append(pts)
                lbl_list.append(lbl)

            # Pad variable-length prompt lists to one tensor
            max_n = max(p.shape[0] for p in pts_list)
            pad_coord = np.array([[-10.0, -10.0]], np.float32)
            for i in range(len(pts_list)):
                need = max_n - pts_list[i].shape[0]
                if need:
                    pts_list[i] = np.vstack([pts_list[i], np.repeat(pad_coord, need, axis=0)])
                    lbl_list[i] = np.hstack([lbl_list[i], np.full(need, -1, np.int64)])

            pts_arr = torch.as_tensor(np.stack(pts_list), device=device)
            lbl_arr = torch.as_tensor(np.stack(lbl_list), device=device)
            boxes_t = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(boxes, np.float32), device=device)

            # IMPORTANT: predict_torch expects coords in the *transformed* (1024-long-side) space.
            orig_hw = (h_p, w_p)
            pts_in = predictor.transform.apply_coords_torch(pts_arr, orig_hw)
            boxes_in = predictor.transform.apply_boxes_torch(boxes_t, orig_hw)

            with torch.inference_mode():
                # returns: (masks_full, iou_preds, low_res_logits)
                _, _, low_res_logits = predictor.predict_torch(
                    point_coords=pts_in,
                    point_labels=lbl_arr,
                    boxes=boxes_in,
                    multimask_output=False,
                    return_logits=True,
                )

            for (r, c), low_res in zip(pts_seed, low_res_logits):
                # Upsample low-resolution logits to crop size
                if low_res.dim() == 2:
                    low_res = low_res.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
                elif low_res.dim() == 3:
                    low_res = low_res.unsqueeze(0)
                logit = F.interpolate(low_res, (h_p, w_p), mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)[0, 0]
                logit = logit.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)

                # Light blur in logit space
                if crop_smooth_sigma > 0:
                    logit = gaussian_filter(logit, crop_smooth_sigma, mode="nearest")

                # CHM boost: compare blurred CHM to seed CHM
                rr, cc = (r - r0), (c - c0)
                seed_h = chm_patch[rr, cc]
                dh = np.clip(chm_blur_p - seed_h, 0, None)  # (h_p, w_p)
                dh_max = float(np.nanmax(dh)) if np.isfinite(dh).any() else 0.0
                if dh_max > 0:
                    logit = logit + (CHM_BOOST * dh / (dh_max + 1e-6)).astype(np.float32)

                seed_rc = (rr, cc)
                prob = prob_from_logit_seedcenter(logit, seed_rc=seed_rc, res=res)
                if np.random.rand() < 0.01:
                    print("seed prob pcts:", np.percentile(prob, [0, 50, 90, 99, 100]))

                # Mosaic max compositing
                prob_mosaic[r0:r1, c0:c1] = np.maximum(prob_mosaic[r0:r1, c0:c1], prob.astype(np.float32))

    # --- Global smoothing and index fusion ---
    prob_mosaic_out = prob_mosaic.copy()  # debug output (pre-smooth mosaic)

    prob_s = smooth_mosaic(prob_mosaic, smooth_sigma)
    prob_s = np.nan_to_num(prob_s, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=0.0).astype(np.float32)
    print("prob_s pcts:", np.nanpercentile(prob_s, [0, 50, 90, 99, 100]))

    base = prob_s * (1 - W_CHM + W_CHM * _norm01(CHM)) * (1 - W_COST + W_COST * (1 - _norm01(COST)))
    z = np.clip(-(CHM - GROUND_THRESH) / SIGMA_GROUND, -60, 60)
    ground_w = (1 / (1 + np.exp(z))) ** W_GROUND

    index = base * ground_w

    # Original: compute min/max BEFORE post smoothing, then normalize AFTER smoothing.
    idx_min = float(np.nanmin(index)) if np.isfinite(index).any() else 0.0
    idx_max = float(np.nanmax(index)) if np.isfinite(index).any() else 1.0

    if post_smooth_sigma > 0:
        index = gaussian_filter(index, post_smooth_sigma, mode="nearest")

    denom = (idx_max - idx_min)
    if not np.isfinite(denom) or denom <= 0:
        index = np.zeros_like(index, dtype=np.float32)
    else:
        index = np.where(
            np.isnan(index),
            NODATA_VAL,
            ((index - idx_min) / (denom + 1e-6)).astype(np.float32),
        )

    if CHM.shape != prob_s.shape or COST.shape != prob_s.shape:
        raise ValueError("CHM/COST shapes do not match SAM prob shape")

    return prob_mosaic_out, prob_s, index, CHM, COST, crs, tfm

def run_tile_proposals(
    records_json: Path,
    out_root: Path,
    ckpt_path: Path,
    *,
    device: str = "cpu",
    rgb_lo_hi=None,
    fast: bool = False,
    fast_batch: int = 32,
    crop_smooth_sigma: float = CROP_SMOOTH_SIGMA,
    smooth_sigma: float = SMOOTH_SIGMA,
    post_smooth_sigma: float = POST_SMOOTH_SIGMA,
):
    """Run SAM proposals from one tile-record file."""
    records_path = Path(records_json)
    if not records_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing records file: {records_path}")

    ckpt = Path(ckpt_path)
    if not ckpt.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing SAM checkpoint: {ckpt}")

    sam = sam_model_registry["vit_l"](checkpoint=str(ckpt))
    sam.to(device).eval()
    predictor = SamPredictor(sam)

    out_dir = out_root / "rasters"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    recs = json.load(open(records_path))
    proposal_records = []

    for rec in recs:
        res = process_chip(
            rec,
            predictor,
            device,
            rgb_lo_hi=rgb_lo_hi,
            fast=fast,
            fast_batch=fast_batch,
            crop_smooth_sigma=crop_smooth_sigma,
            smooth_sigma=smooth_sigma,
            post_smooth_sigma=post_smooth_sigma,
        )
        if res is None:
            continue

        mosaic_prob, prob_s, index, chm_out, cost_out, crs, tfm = res
        name = f"{rec['tile']}_{rec['chip_id']}"

        _check_sam_outputs(prob_s, name)

        meta = {
            "driver": "GTiff",
            "height": index.shape[0],
            "width": index.shape[1],
            "count": 1,
            "dtype": "float32",
            "crs": crs,
            "transform": tfm,
            "compress": "deflate",
        }

        with rasterio.open(out_dir / f"{name}_logit.tif", "w", **meta) as dst:
            dst.write(mosaic_prob.astype(np.float32), 1)
        with rasterio.open(out_dir / f"{name}_sam_prob.tif", "w", **meta) as dst:
            dst.write(prob_s.astype(np.float32), 1)
        with rasterio.open(out_dir / f"{name}_sam_index.tif", "w", **meta) as dst:
            dst.write(index.astype(np.float32), 1)
        with rasterio.open(out_dir / f"{name}_chm.tif", "w", **meta) as dst:
            dst.write(chm_out.astype(np.float32), 1)
        with rasterio.open(out_dir / f"{name}_cost.tif", "w", **meta) as dst:
            dst.write(cost_out.astype(np.float32), 1)

        proposal_records.append(
            {
                "file_name": str((out_dir / f"{name}_sam_prob.tif").resolve()),
                "chm": str((out_dir / f"{name}_chm.tif").resolve()),
                "cost": str((out_dir / f"{name}_cost.tif").resolve()),
                "logit": str((out_dir / f"{name}_logit.tif").resolve()),
                "index": str((out_dir / f"{name}_sam_index.tif").resolve()),
                "mask": "",
                "meta": {
                    "crs": crs.to_wkt() if crs else None,
                    "transform": list(tfm) if tfm is not None else None,
                },
            }
        )

    out_json = out_root / "proposal_records.json"
    with open(out_json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(proposal_records, f)
    print(f"✓ wrote proposal outputs ({len(proposal_records)} records)")

def smooth_mosaic(prob_mosaic: np.ndarray, sigma_px: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Smooth probabilities with valid-mask normalization for sparse coverage."""
    prob_blur = gaussian_filter(prob_mosaic, sigma_px, mode="nearest")
    val_mask = (prob_mosaic > 0).astype(np.float32)
    val_blur = gaussian_filter(val_mask, sigma_px, mode="nearest")
    prob_s = np.where(val_blur == 0, np.nan, prob_blur / val_blur)
    return np.clip(prob_s, 0, 1)

def stretch_u8_percentile(arr: np.ndarray, p_lo: float = 2.0, p_hi: float = 98.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Robust percentile stretch to uint8 (single channel)."""
    arr = np.asarray(arr, np.float32)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    if not finite.any():
        return np.zeros_like(arr, dtype=np.uint8)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(arr[finite], (p_lo, p_hi))
    if not np.isfinite(lo) or not np.isfinite(hi) or hi <= lo:
        return np.zeros_like(arr, dtype=np.uint8)
    out = (arr - lo) * 255.0 / (hi - lo + 1e-9)
    return np.clip(out, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
